baseline_models.mechanism: The speakers assign a light, spreading, agitated causality to the messengers, then reverse the direction of agency by promising a concrete harmful impact from themselves.

activation_trace.role: Dispersion after light movement gives the alleged omen the shape of a harm imagined to spread from the messengers.
Released agitation and impulsiveness expose volatility in the act of ominous attribution itself.
An effect that reaches and afflicts turns diffuse suspicion into a promised, directed injury.

changed_reading.before: The crowd blames the messengers for bad luck and threatens them.
changed_reading.after: The crowd projects its own volatility outward as a spreading omen, then openly takes ownership of the concrete harm it plans to send back.

baseline_models.mechanism: Circulating accusation becomes an ultimatum, verbal pelting or expulsion, and finally bodily pain; the verse stages collective violence as a progression rather than a single threat.

activation_trace.role: Speech circulating among people supplies the social medium through which the charge becomes collective.
Forcible restraint gives the ultimatum its first operational aim: stop the messengers' activity.
Hurtful words figured as stones make abusive speech an early phase of the threatened assault.
Cursing, expulsion, and exclusion extend the mechanism from insult to removal from the community.
Punitive infliction names the intended result of the escalating social and bodily pressure.
Pain imposed on another fixes the endpoint in the victims' felt bodies.

changed_reading.before: The crowd issues two roughly synonymous threats.
changed_reading.after: The crowd lays out an escalation ladder: suppress the message, pelt with speech or stones, expel, and ensure that the sanction is physically felt.

baseline_models.mechanism: A speculative omen charge is converted by collective speech into a self-authorized verdict and sentence; accusation, command, and sanction are compressed into one mob proceeding.

activation_trace.role: Speech used to impose judgment on another supplies the crowd's assumed jurisdiction.
Guessing about the unseen exposes the evidentiary weakness of the omen charge beneath the confident verdict.
Prohibition converts an unsupported diagnosis into an enforceable-looking order.
Punishment completes the crowd's imitation of judicial authority.

changed_reading.before: The crowd angrily threatens unwelcome preachers.
changed_reading.after: The crowd stages a counterfeit court in which conjectural causation is treated as proof and the accusers appoint themselves judge and executioner.

baseline_models.mechanism: The demanded cessation is spatialized as forcing the messengers to an endpoint, while expulsion, gathered stones, and punitive deprivation remove both their message and bodies from the shared field.

activation_trace.role: A terminal limit turns 'desist' into an imposed endpoint for the messengers' movement and mission.
Gathered stones and the stone-marked grave materialize the terminal enclosure threatened by the crowd.
Restraint, withholding, and forced abstention add social deprivation to the threatened endpoint.
The threatened endpoint is not abstract: its harmful effect is made to reach the addressees.

changed_reading.before: The condition asks only that the messengers stop speaking.
changed_reading.after: The condition seeks a total endpoint: silence, removal, deprivation, and possibly a stone-marked final enclosure.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediate answer repeats the omen root, relocates the 'bird' to the accusers, and places rejected reminder beside excess; projected causality is returned to its speakers.

activation_trace.role: A spreading, mobile omen is the causal burden initially placed on the messengers.
The same dispersive bird image is repeated in a construction that returns its attachment to the accusers.
Restoring something to awareness makes reminder, and the reaction to it, the scene of the alleged omen.
Exceeding a limit supplies an internal diagnosis for the crowd's harmful trajectory.

structural_cues: 36:19 directly answers 36:18 with the same ط ي ر root in طائركم معكم.
The interruption أئن ذكرتم is followed by بل أنتم قوم مسرفون.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies lexical repetition, 'with you,' reminder, and excess; I infer that responsibility is being relocated from the messengers to the speakers' response. A live alternative is a narrower denial of omen without a full causal diagnosis.

changed_reading.before: The messengers' arrival carries an external bad omen.
changed_reading.after: The supposed omen is the crowd's own exceeded-limit response to being reminded, projected onto the messengers and then returned to its source.

context_deltas.mechanism: Earlier images of bound posture, barriers on both sides, covering, and failed sight turn the demand that the messengers stop into an externalization of blocked reception.

activation_trace.role: Forcible stopping is the action the crowd wants imposed on the message-bearers.
A collar that binds an organ supplies bodily restriction behind the crowd's rigid reception.
Barriers closing gaps on both sides model a channel in which the warning cannot pass.
A covering that conceals the object supplies the obscured perceptual surface.
Literal seeing marks the capacity declared ineffective after the barriers and covering.

structural_cues: 36:8-9 accumulate bodily restraint and barriers before stating that they do not see.
36:10 makes warning and non-warning equal for those who do not believe.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies closure imagery and ineffective warning; I infer a causal arrow from blocked reception to coercively demanding that the sender cease. The alternative is that the closure describes a settled consequence rather than the crowd's psychology.

changed_reading.before: The crowd asks the messengers to stop an activity it dislikes.
changed_reading.after: Unable or unwilling to open its own reception channel, the crowd attempts to solve that blockage by stopping the incoming message.

context_deltas.mechanism: The crowd commandeers the conditional form of warning: a message meant to awaken caution, complete delivery, and enable protection and mercy is answered by an ultimatum meant to terminate delivery and inflict pain.

activation_trace.role: The crowd's prohibition supplies the coercive counter-command to the messengers' warning.
Punitive pain is the crowd's intended endpoint for its version of warning.
Warning that frightens in order to awaken caution supplies the protective function being inverted.
Bringing a message to its recipient defines the messengers' limited duty that the ultimatum seeks to halt.
Repelling harm through protection supplies the beneficial aim of the surah's other conditional warning.
Merciful tenderness is the hoped-for outcome that contrasts with the crowd's promised pain.

structural_cues: 36:17 limits the messengers' responsibility to clear delivery immediately before the crowd's ultimatum.
36:45 also joins an imperative concerning danger to a prospective outcome, but its outcome is mercy.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies two warning structures and opposed outcomes; I infer that 36:18 mimics and weaponizes the messenger's communicative form. A live alternative is that the similarity is ordinary conditional-threat grammar without deliberate parody.

changed_reading.before: The crowd simply warns the messengers of punishment.
changed_reading.after: The crowd hijacks warning grammar, reversing a caution ordered toward protection into a counter-warning ordered toward silencing and pain.

context_deltas.mechanism: A purposeful man crosses the city, follows the messengers, and declares belief; the abrupt sequence into entry, forgiveness, and honor denies the threatening collective's claim that consequences finally come 'from us.'

activation_trace.role: The crowd claims it can make a harmful consequence reach dissenting bodies.
Punitive infliction names the outcome the crowd claims to control.
Purposeful movement toward a sought end makes the man's intervention an active crossing of social pressure.
Following in another's track supplies the allegiance publicly opposed to the crowd's demand.
Heart-settling assent gives the dissenting declaration its inner counterweight to ominous agitation.
Passage into an interior marks a new destination immediately after the declaration.
Protective covering of fault supplies an outcome opposite to exposed punitive injury.
Bestowed honor reverses the degradation intended by expulsion and pelting.

structural_cues: 36:20-25 move from the farthest city edge to a public declaration of belief.
36:26 follows that declaration immediately with 'It was said: enter the garden,' then 36:27 names forgiveness and honor.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies sequence but does not state how the transition to entry occurs; I infer only that the crowd's claimed control over final outcomes is broken, not that a particular unreported act caused the transition. The alternative is an unspecified transition unrelated to enactment of the threat.

changed_reading.before: The phrase 'from us' makes the crowd the effective source and controller of the threatened end.
changed_reading.after: The crowd may control immediate social force, but the adjacent dissent-to-honor sequence places final consequence outside its jurisdiction.

context_deltas.mechanism: The crowd's cumulative, person-directed threat is answered by no descending army but a single cry that extinguishes, and the later repeated cry takes people while they are still disputing.

activation_trace.role: Things piled one on another give the crowd's threatened violence a cumulative, many-against-few force.
Collectively circulating speech supplies the many-voiced threat that the later single cry compresses.
Descent and arrival are explicitly negated for any host, stripping the response of massed force.
One alarming cry concentrates the answering force into a single sonic event.
Singularity sharply opposes the crowd's collective accumulation.
Life or awareness becoming still after motion supplies the terminal reversal of the crowd's coercive energy.
Active contention places the later seizure inside ongoing adversarial speech.

structural_cues: 36:28 denies that a host descended after the man, and 36:29 reduces the event to one cry.
36:49 repeats the one-cry pattern while its objects are disputing.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies adjacency, singular cry, extinguishing, and later disputation; I infer an ironic directional reversal of the crowd's threat. The live alternative is that these are broader judgment scenes rather than a pointed answer to the wording of 36:18.

changed_reading.before: A collective can accumulate speech, stones, and pain to silence a few messengers.
changed_reading.after: The many-voiced threat prefigures its own reversal: no massed force is needed, and one cry can terminate the disputing collective's entire escalation.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus's self-sourced painful sanction is later counterposed to peace delivered as a saying from a merciful Lord; source, speech, and felt outcome form two opposed chains.

activation_trace.role: Uttered speech launches the crowd's chain from declaration to threatened pain.
Pain imposed on another is the outcome attached to the crowd's self-declared source.
Freedom from harm supplies the exact experiential opposite of painful touching.
Uttered saying becomes the vehicle of peace rather than threat.
True lordship and sovereignty identify a source that contrasts with the crowd's self-authorized 'from us.'
Tender mercy determines the quality of the source and the peaceful outcome of its speech.

structural_cues: 36:18 joins the speakers' قالوا to مِّنَّا عذاب أليم.
36:58 condenses سلام قولا من رب رحيم into a contrasting source-speech-outcome formula.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies conspicuous lexical and source-formula echoes; I infer a designed opposition between two speech regimes. The alternative is a thematic contrast without a tight syntactic correspondence.

changed_reading.before: The threat is a local hostile utterance.
changed_reading.after: The threat belongs to a counterfeit speech regime in which a collective claims lordlike control and emits pain, later answered by authoritative speech whose emitted condition is peace.

context_deltas.mechanism: The crowd's mouth turns conjectural blame into punishment, but the later judgment separates parties, seals mouths, and lets bodily members testify to earned action; assertion is replaced by embodied evidence.

activation_trace.role: Speech arrogating judgment supplies the unsupported tribunal that later evidence reverses.
Conjecture about an unseen cause marks the crowd's accusation as assertion without secure evidence.
Reciprocal recompense ties consequence to action rather than to projected omen.
Separation until parties are distinct supplies an adjudicative sorting absent from mob accusation.
A preventive seal disables the mouth that could continue self-serving assertion.
The mouth's opening for speech identifies the channel that is specifically closed.
Intelligible speech moves from the partisan mouth to the hands as a new evidentiary channel.
Knowledge-based declaration supplies testimony in place of ominous conjecture.
Acquired action provides the object of testimony and the basis of consequence.

structural_cues: 36:54 explicitly denies wrong and links recompense to what was done.
36:59 separates the offenders, and 36:65 seals mouths while hands speak and feet testify.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a later evidentiary procedure; I infer that it exposes the focus scene as counterfeit adjudication because its omen charge moves straight from assertion to sentence. The alternative is a general eschatological contrast rather than a direct forensic reply.

changed_reading.before: The crowd's confident collective assertion is treated as sufficient proof for punishment.
changed_reading.after: The focus becomes an anti-trial whose conjecture and self-issued sentence are later overturned by separation, action-based recompense, and bodily testimony.

context_deltas.mechanism: The threatening utterance is placed within a wider speech hierarchy: forgetful human disputation challenges creation, while authoritative command brings the intended thing into being.

activation_trace.role: Ordinary utterance is the crowd's instrument for attempting to control other people.
Judgmental speech shows the crowd extending ordinary utterance into a claim of effective rule.
Adversarial disputation identifies the broader human speech posture into which the focus threat fits.
Loss of remembered origin supplies the epistemic gap from which confident dispute speaks.
The human challenge is explicitly emitted as speech, aligning it with the focus's coercive declaration.
Binding command supplies authority that is effective without mob enforcement.
A thing's saying as effective indication sharpens the contrast between merely coercive and reality-altering speech.
Occurrence and presence in time supply the realized endpoint of the final command.

structural_cues: 36:77-78 move from a created human to a manifest disputant who forgets his creation and speaks a challenge.
36:82 closes the argument with command, saying, and immediate becoming.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated قال and an explicit contrast between human dispute and effective command; I infer a hierarchy of speech-power that bounds the crowd's threat. The alternative is that the final creation formula answers only the resurrection dispute, not the earlier coercive speech.

changed_reading.before: The crowd's declaration appears performatively powerful because it can mobilize collective violence.
changed_reading.after: Its speech can coerce socially but cannot govern reality; it belongs to forgetful dispute and is bounded by a command whose saying and realization coincide.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because the translation branch of ر ج م is remote from the surface threat of stoning. It remains anchored in the threatened verb and is activated by repeated clear-delivery cues, but downstream prose must present it only as a hostile-recoding mechanism, never as the lexical translation of لنرجمنكم.

activation_trace.role: Rendering speech into another tongue supplies an exploratory image for the crowd's coercive recoding of the message.
Successful delivery of a message supplies the input that the crowd recodes as an omen and offense.
Meaning disclosed by speech or sign establishes the clarity that hostile recoding distorts.
Recitation and reading renew the clear communicative object that rejection translates into social danger.
Disclosure of meaning again contrasts with the crowd's hostile reinterpretive operation.

changed_reading.before: The crowd threatens to stone the messengers for their clear proclamation.
changed_reading.after: Before any stone is thrown, the crowd performs a hostile 'translation': clear delivery is recoded as contagious omen, and the messengers are recoded from warners into punishable causes.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This activation uses the packet's non-dominant ق ل ل target for the focus root ق و ل, so it is deliberately form-distant. Its trembling and instability images align visibly with the focus's ط ي ر agitation and remain anchored to قالوا, but they should qualify the crowd's speech posture rather than replace the normal sense 'they said.'

activation_trace.role: A tremor from fear or anger gives the collective utterance an embodied instability beneath its certainty.
Movement with little stability makes the speech an attempt to stabilize a shaken group.
Impulsive agitation supplies the matching volatility that the speakers project onto the messengers.
Stillness after motion provides a severe later counter-image to the crowd's agitated utterance.

changed_reading.before: A confident collective calmly announces its diagnosis and sanction.
changed_reading.after: The certainty of 'they said' may mask a collective tremor: unstable, agitated speech seeks equilibrium by naming the messengers as the source of instability.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is cross-domain because it activates the sweet-water and abstention branches inside عذاب rather than treating them as alternate dictionary meanings of punishment. The focus anchors it through عذاب and the threatened reaching effect, while the surah's springs, fruit, and mercy make resource deprivation materially thinkable; downstream prose must mark it as a social mechanism of punishment, not a translation claim.

activation_trace.role: Sweet, wholesome water supplies the valued good whose loss can make punishment materially felt.
Withholding and forced abstention turn punitive power into exclusion from sustaining goods.
A reaching harmful effect explains how social exclusion becomes embodied pain.
A flowing spring supplies the shared life-support resource against which deprivation becomes legible.
Ripe fruit adds nourishment to the material commons potentially controlled by a hostile community.
Merciful tenderness supplies the opposing mode by which vulnerable life is preserved rather than deprived.

changed_reading.before: Painful punishment means direct assault alone.
changed_reading.after: The crowd's 'from us' may also claim control over access: punishment can touch by expulsion and withholding the sweet water and nourishment through which bodies remain in communal life.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: The grave image is a legitimate branch of ر ج م but goes beyond the verse's explicit report, since the packet never says the threat was enacted. It remains anchored to لنرجمنكم and becomes live when later speech joins bones, decay, and renewed creation; render it as the threat's imagined finality being denied, not as a narrated death.

activation_trace.role: Gathered stones, grave stones, and the grave give the threat an imagined stone-marked finality.
Hard bone supplies what remains after the body's apparent ending.
Decay and worn remains intensify the apparent irreversibility of the grave endpoint.
Bringing a thing into being breaks the claim that stone, bone, and decay can impose a final terminus.

changed_reading.before: Stoning is the crowd's ultimate means of making the messengers disappear.
changed_reading.after: The threat imagines a stone-marked endpoint, while the later bone-and-recreation sequence denies that communal violence can make such an endpoint final.

strongest_changes: The immediate طائركم معكم reply returns the projected omen to the speakers and links it to rejected reminder and excess.
The crowd's ultimatum hijacks warning grammar, reversing protection and mercy into suppression and pain.
No descending host but one cry reverses the crowd's cumulative, many-voiced threat.
سلام قولا من رب رحيم forms an opposed source-speech-outcome chain to the crowd's self-sourced painful sanction.
Later embodied testimony exposes the focus scene as a counterfeit tribunal built on conjecture.
summary.what_was_special: The whole-surah packet repeatedly changed 36:18 through reversals of source, direction, speech authority, and evidence: projected harm returns to the projector, coercive warning is answered by merciful warning, many voices by one cry, mob judgment by bodily testimony, and claimed finality by renewed creation.
remaining_uncertainties: The adjacency of 36:25-27 does not specify the mechanism of transition into the garden, so it cannot prove enactment of the threat.
The legal, hostile-translation, resource-deprivation, and grave mechanisms are branch activations, not lexical replacements for the surface wording.
The non-dominant ق ل ل activation is deliberately form-distant and should remain a qualified description of speech posture.
